The physics in this game are broken. The ball goes in a random direction whenever the paddle hits it and sometimes the paddle goes straight through the ball. It's not possible to play this game properly as-is. Requested a refund.

[h1]Your ball goes through your racket.[/h1]

The narcoleptic polling rate of the physics engine here means that, by the time the game registers the coordinates of your ball relative to your racket, it'll give you one of the three following results:

[olist][*]Register collision with the [b][i]back[/i][/b] of your racket, sending the ball screaming into your own net.

[*]Limp slowly into the middle of the field to time out and count against you as a "dead ball", with its own explicit score penalty as well as adding to your time penalty.

[*]Clip through your racket altogether.[/olist]

This leads to a meta-game where you need to thread the needle and play [i]around[/i] this game's busted collision-detection and hit the ball with all of the zeal of an octogenarian on bingo night while trying your best not to agitate its lumbago.

Good luck getting a shutout when even a normal Hard run can get utterly derailed by this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

At least on Valve Index, this game's busted. I don't know what kind of polling rate you need to track the fastest moving part of a controller and make sure collision detection never "drops the ball", but if Beat Saber's devs can discover wrist flicks adding more acceleration than they initially tested for and then correct with a patch, this dev can too.

Requested a refund.

[b][i][u]Update[/u]: Learned that, even with 1.1hrs of playtime, I cannot refund this purchase since it was purchased more than two weeks ago (two months to the day).

Guess they get to keep my money.[/i][/b]

This tries to be both a sim and an arcade, by inheriting the bad parts of both.

It's not fun to play like an arcade, but tedious like a sim. Sets are short, you either win or lose in just a few hits. There are log pauses between sets. The paddles need to be lined up perfectly.

It's not challenging like a sim, but simple like an arcade. The paddles are transparent (how the hell do you improve if you can't see what you're doing). There's no replay to figure out what to do better. The speed ramps up so fast that you have to rely on expertise (which you can not gain). There's no training mode (there's a Zen mode but that is completely different from the rest of the game).

Although I've only played about 35 minutes, this is a fantastic game! I bought it to try and give myself some inspiration to work out and get in shape, and this game lets me build up a sweat and get up a good workout that's amazingly fun! 

I second the comments about using the wriststraps though. So far I've not had many problems, but so far I've only played Easy (it's early days for me!) One thing I'd add for newer VR users is to keep your thumb away from the Menu button when you grip the controllers. I've had the game pause without warning when I inadvertently pressed the button during play, which was distracting to say the least.

Easy mode is fun, but make no mistake, it's challenging. Rather than 5 levels of the same difficulty, the AI gets bonuses at the start of each new round, making their returns faster, or their speed faster, and you can feel the difference. There's also a Zen mode, which just lets you whack the ball around and bounce it off the walls, and which is very good to cool down after a workout (and sharpen your skills for the next day!)

There's very little running around in this game, but you WILL jump and squat to get those high/low balls, so if you're playing in a small space, make sure it's very clear before you start.

The only gripe I have is the backgrounds. They're great and they fit in, but it would be nice if we could play Holoball in some different surroundings.

This was a decent game back in the day when the Vive was released, but now I would not recommend it.  The game mechanics are really dangerous, as you end up diving to get balls right at the edge of your playspace.  There are ways to try to mitigate it (ex: setting smaller bounds), but the fast pacing of the game prevents any of them from working 100%.  It can be scary watching someone play this!  

This is probably one of the absolute riskiest VR games to play, potentially leading to a broken controller or worse (it was common to read horror stories related to this game in the first months after the Vive released).  In the last couple of years better racket games have been released with designs that don't present the same risk of collateral damage, so I would suggest going with one of those instead.  

If you do choose to play this game, make sure your TV/monitor is behind you, your bounds are set accurately, and your health insurance is paid up!

这个游戏是一款健身类的VR游戏，健身减肥必备。进入游戏界面的时候,会有一种错觉,好像进入到了一款枪击游戏和反恐游戏。整个背景色是非常浓郁的黑色,难以程度选择项则是非常显眼跳跃的荧光亮色系。我第一次置身其中时,感觉身处的环境很诡异，整个游戏里的环境看起来有点复古的味道,像很早的电子风格,音乐搭配的也恰到到处,有节奏点,会让你有运动起来的欲望。初次体验,选择最简单的EASY模式。第一次玩的时候,会有两种感觉,明明感觉自己接住了球,为什么显示没接住。对手玩家为什么那么厉害,常常以5:0的大优势分分钟结束游戏。开始游戏后,会进入到一个封闭的环境中,头顶上就是记录分数的显示牌。之后在你的前方会出现一个球,你手上拿的Vive手柄也会变成一个球拍,这个时候你就可以用你的球拍去打你的球,当球撞击到墙面或地面的时候会进行反弹,反弹多次,这个球就已经输掉啦。这款游戏就是将你的球打入对方的门里,并且要接住对手打给你的球,对手就是对面墙上的红方块,当你打出一些快速度的球或者一些高难度的球时,它就会产生纰漏,而你将获得一分。游戏的赛点是五,如果你先拿到五分,就可以进入到下一局。游戏的玩法十分简单,没什么特别的要求,也不需要什么特殊的技能,每晋级一关,球的速度会加快,游戏会越来越激烈,难度也会增加。所以,这款游戏看似容易,其实也在考验着你的运动细胞。在玩这款游戏的时候所处的房间一定不要有障碍物!一定不要有障碍物!一定不要有障碍物!重要的事情说三遍。手柄撞到飞出去事小,自己磕到撞到事大。一定要说的就是这款游戏真的非常耗费体力,与真实生活中打羽毛球、网球等运动无异。当你发现越用力的击球,球越容易“破门而入”取得胜利,就会情不自禁的用尽全身力气来打球。我是用大朋E3定位版VR头盔玩的，常常打完几局后就已经满头大汗,筋疲力尽。所以特别锻炼身体。

This game is so close to being perfect.  For the first hour, I was in love with this game.  It was after the first hour that the issues began to arise.  The first is that the AI shoots the ball right on the edge of the play space.  Now, they do have a way to add padding to your play space to keep you from hitting walls, and that's a great thing to have, but when the AI is consistently throwing shots that make you fearful of hitting a wall (I hit a picture frame and smashed the glass) it stops being fun.  Tweaking the AI to keep it from throwing so many shots on the play space line would go a long way.

The other issue is the physics of the ball.  They're just not right.  Hit the ball to the left, and it curves to the right.  It does all these weird curves that make absolutely no sense and make it difficult to have any sort of strategy.  Why try to hit the ball in one direction when it's just going to fly off in the direction it wants to anyway?  That might have to do with the way the paddles are angled in relation to the controllers.  You can't hold the controllers normally and have the paddles be at a normal angle.  It's odd.  Allowing the user to modify the angle of the paddles would be nice.

Overall, fun game.  But if you have a small play area or are looking for a paddle ball game where you can actually control the direction of the ball, look elsewhere.  Though I'm recommending it, I do so with reservations.
